sites.functional_impact_measured: Methotrexate binding and uptake assayed; insertion had minor effects on both — classified as functionally tolerated.
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly names Pro-297 as the insertion site in the external loop between TM7 and TM8. Python confirms residue 297 = P (match) and residue 298 = T. The site sits 9 aa from the TM7 C-boundary (288) and 11 aa from the TM8 N-boundary (308), well clear of both TM helices. The construct is full-length and membrane-anchored (EGFP-fused), and methotrexate binding and uptake were both measured and found only minimally affected. Full-length hRFC fused to EGFP at the C-terminus, with HA epitope inserted at Pro-297 in the extracellular loop between TM7 and TM8 (EC loop 289-307), expressed in mammalian cells and assayed for methotrexate binding and uptake. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The hemagglutinin epitope insertion mutants were also tested for their effects on the function of the reduced folate carrier. For these studies, each of the constructs had a carboxyl-terminal fusion of the enhanced green fluorescent protein to monitor and quantitate expression. Insertions into the external loop between transmembrane regions 7 and 8 (Pro-297), the cytoplasmic loop between transmembrane regions 6 and 7 (Ser-225), and near the cytoplasmic amino and carboxyl termini (Pro-20 and Gly-492, respectively) had minor effects on methotrexate binding and uptake.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Methotrexate binding was preserved but uptake was selectively interfered with — function_perturbed; the tag reaches the cell surface but disrupts transport activity.
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly names Pro-427 as the insertion site in the external loop between TM11 and TM12. Python confirms residue 427 = P (match) and residue 428 = V. The site sits 9 aa from the TM11 C-boundary (418) and 5 aa from the TM12 N-boundary (432), satisfying the ≥3 aa TM-distance constraint. However, the paper reports that this insertion selectively interfered with methotrexate uptake (while binding was preserved), indicating the tag perturbs transport function at this position; ranked lower than site 1. Full-length hRFC with HA epitope inserted at Pro-427 in the extracellular loop between TM11 and TM12 (EC loop 419-431), expressed in mammalian cells and assayed for methotrexate binding and uptake. [validation: function_perturbed; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The insertion into the cytoplasmic loop between transmembrane regions 10 and 11 (Gln-385) greatly reduced both binding and uptake of methotrexate, whereas the insertion into the external loop between transmembrane regions 11 and 12 (Pro-427) selectively interfered with uptake but not binding.

literature_notes: Six other ledger sites were evaluated and excluded because they are intracellular: L1 Ser-225 (IC loop TM6-7, 204-268), L1 Pro-20 (IC N-terminus, 1-27), L1 Gly-492 (IC C-terminus, 453-591), L2 Gln-385 (paper numbering off-by-one; Q is at 386 in the IC loop 386-397, not extracellular), L3 C-terminal HA (IC C-terminus 453-591), L4/L5 HA after Glu226 (IC loop 204-268), L4/L6 Myc-His10 after Leu537 (IC C-terminus 453-591). L7 (SLC19A-HA) names no insertion position and cannot be pinned. L8 (BRIL at N-terminus of TM1, nanobody at C-terminus of TM12) places both fusions on the intracellular face per the authoritative topology landmarks (N-terminus 1-27 is IC; C-terminus of TM12 leads into IC region 453-591). No extracellular N-terminal terminus exists for SLC19A1 (residues 1-27 are intracellular). The two sites reported are the only ledger-grounded extracellular insertion sites.
